days.notes: Progression concept: first 12 km is tempo steady-state, final 2 km adds intensity without full tempo effort. Teaches body to run faster when tired.

days.notes: Second quality session (3 days after Friday intervals). Longer tempo (6 km) than week 1, preparing for sustained marathon-pace efforts.

weeks.weekly_summary: RECOVERY WEEK: Volume reduced 20% to 35 km (from 44 km week 3). Long run cut to 11 km (20% reduction). One quality session maintained. Focus: consolidate adaptations, reduce fatigue, prepare for next block.
weeks.coaching_notes: Week 4 is a structured recovery week. Total volume drops from 44 km to 35 km (20% reduction). Long run shrinks from 14 km to 11 km. One tempo session is preserved to maintain intensity signals, but intensity is slightly modulated — shorter and less aggressive than peak week. Easy runs are slightly reduced. This is a critical adaptation window: the body consolidates improvements during recovery, not during hard training. Athlete should feel fresher by week's end, ready for the next 4-week block (Aerobic Development → Peak Training as they approach marathon race date).
recovery_flags: Monitor sleep quality — recovery weeks are when adaptation happens.
Consider doing extra foam rolling or massage this week.
Hydration and nutrition should remain consistent despite lower volume.
weeks.next_week_preview: Next 4-week block (weeks 5–8) transitions to Aerobic Development. Expect higher long-run volumes (15–18 km), progression runs with marathon-pace segments, and potential shift toward 1–2 quality sessions per week with slightly higher intensity. Plan assumes race is 8+ weeks away from week 5 start.

coaching_overview: This 4-week Base Building block establishes a robust aerobic foundation for marathon training. Starting from recent Strava data (22.8 km over 3 runs in 2 weeks, 6:45 easy pace, 5:56 tempo estimate), the plan progressively builds volume from 38 km (week 1) to a peak of 44 km (week 3), then recovers to 35 km (week 4). Total 4-week volume: 158 km. All sessions use exact paces derived from current fitness: 6:45–6:50/km for easy runs, 5:56/km for tempo, 5:40–5:45/km for VO2 max intervals. The 80/20 polarization is maintained across all four weeks. Two quality sessions per week are distributed to avoid consecutive hard days and to allow adequate recovery. Long run grows progressively (10 → 12 → 14 → 11 km), respecting the 1–2 km weekly growth rule. Week 4 is a structured recovery week, reducing volume 20% and long run by 20%, with one tempo session preserved to maintain aerobic stimulus. The athlete operates comfortably within the 7-hour weekly time budget (averaging ~6.25 hours/week). Upon completion, the athlete will be well-prepared to enter the Aerobic Development block (weeks 5–8) with longer long runs (15–18 km), progression runs at marathon pace, and continued polarized structure. No specific race date is set; progression to Peak Training (VO2 max focus, marathon-pace segments) and Taper will follow once a race date is confirmed.
